query: Which material can be used for to improve the ductility and toughness of the HfZrTi high-entropy alloy (HEAs), and why?

generation.hypothesis: Adding a small fraction of niobium to HfZrTi high-entropy alloys will improve ductility and toughness by refining the microstructure and facilitating plastic deformation.
generation.material_initial_state: HfZrTi high-entropy alloy in homogenized form with baseline mechanical properties.
generation.intervention: Incorporation of approximately 5–10 atomic percent niobium into the HfZrTi alloy composition.
generation.conditions: Melt the HfZrTi alloy with niobium under high-purity inert or vacuum conditions, followed by homogenization at elevated temperature and subsequent controlled cooling.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a stable Nb-containing solid-solution phase that reduces local lattice distortion.
generation.mechanism: Nb addition alters atomic bonding characteristics and lattice parameters, reducing defect formation and enhancing the mobility of dislocations for improved ductility and toughness.
generation.predicted_outcome: Moderate increase in ductility and fracture toughness relative to undoped HfZrTi, as measured by tensile and impact tests.
generation.baseline: Undoped HfZrTi alloy with moderate ductility and toughness at ambient conditions.
generation.boundary: Optimal Nb content and processing conditions need to be experimentally determined; excessive Nb content may introduce brittle phases.
generation.uncertainty: No direct experimental data or references were provided to confirm the exact doping level or final property improvements.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare multiple alloy samples with varying Nb content (e.g., 0%, 5%, 10%, and 15% at.% Nb) using vacuum arc melting, followed by the same heat treatment schedule.
measurements: Tensile properties (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation) at room temperature
Plane-strain fracture toughness (KIC) measurements to evaluate impact on toughness
Microstructural characterizations (SEM, XRD) to observe phase changes and grain refinement
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If added Nb does not improve or significantly reduces ductility and toughness compared to baseline HfZrTi, the hypothesis is falsified.
